Kim / team — quick technical notes to include in the runbook and declaration draft. I'll prepare the CAIQ crosswalk in the next 24 hours.

1) KMS partitioning
- We provision customer-managed key rings per region (EU key rings stored in EU HSM/KMS tenancy). Keys are not replicated to APAC; they remain in the primary region unless the customer explicitly requests key export (which requires legal approvals).
- For Private (VPC) deployments we support a dedicated KMS key per customer per region and provide logs for key access (integrated into audit stream).

2) Standby peering model (high level)
- Primary: EU private deployment with direct VPC peering to the customer's VPC (primary path).
- Standby: APAC private cluster can be configured as an idle/standby with private peering established but routes withdrawn (BGP route control) until a manual or automated failover is triggered.
- Failover triggers: configuration flag + health probes + control-plane failover. During standby we do not replicate persistent KV cache or model ephemeral tokens to the standby cluster to avoid cross-region residency of sensitive caches.

3) Data locality and logs
- Request/response tokens for inference remain in-region for primary processing. Audit logs and system metrics can be replicated to central telemetry if you opt in; default is region-local storage for logs containing PII.

4) Deliverables I'll attach: kms-partitioning-guidelines.pdf and VPC-Standby-Peering-Runbook-Redwood-20270217.docx. Also drafting CAIQ control mappings for your spreadsheet items.

LMK if you need a more prescriptive failover SLA — current standby mode is intended for DR with manual/automated promotion but not active-active processing.

— Rishi
